policy: Review every closed candidate set. Select only when ASV wording or an explicit mapped textual note distinguishes a reading; otherwise mark underdetermined and retain the base fallback. The base candidate is the qere, which is what MACULA Hebrew projects; the alternative is the ketiv written in the Leningrad Codex.

decisions.evidence: ASV renders the qere noun as 'all my calamity'; the ketiv reading is not reflected in the supplied English.
ASV main text 'ye are nothing' reflects ketiv לא; the mapped textual-variant note assigns qere לו to the other reading, 'are like thereto.'
ASV explicitly renders the qere imperative with 'return again'; the Hebrew-gloss note concerns 'my righteousness is in it,' not this unit.
